title: [finding] delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts is a real end-to-end proof of the ADR-0091 validity window, and no authz matrix row cites it
body:
Found while implementing #8811 (which adds the `grant-validity-window` row to `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts`). Filed unassigned; observation-class.

**The proof exists and is unclaimed.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts` boots a real stack and, in its own header's words, asserts the RESOLUTION path: "the delegate RESOLVES the delegated position while inside the validity window and STOPS resolving it at `valid_until` — the L1 resolution-time filter, on the real persisted row, via the real `resolveAuthzContext`". That is a direct end-to-end exercise of the ADR-0091 D1/D2 window on `sys_user_position`, which is exactly the primitive #8811's row records.

It carries an ADR-0054 liveness id (`@proof: delegation-of-duty`) but **no** `// authz-row:` header line, because until #8811 no matrix row existed to claim it.

**Why #8811 did not cite it.** Under the #7976 mutual-attribution contract a cited proof file must name the citing row back, so adding `proof: 'delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts'` to the row requires a one-line edit in that proof file. That is outside #8811's declared file surface (the matrix plus its ledger check), so the row instead records in its note that the proof exists and is uncited. Nothing is wrong today — the row is sound without a proof because it is deliberately not in `HIGH_RISK` (that list marks primitives guarding object data through a sibling HTTP entry point; this one guards grant derivation).

**What the work is.** Two lines, both mechanical:

1. add `// authz-row: grant-validity-window` to the proof file's header;
2. add `proof: 'delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts'` to the `grant-validity-window` row.

`checkLedger` asserts the pairing in both directions, so the change is self-verifying — and it upgrades the row from "unit-proven, e2e exists but uncited" to a cited end-to-end proof, which is the honest upgrade path the row's own note names.

**Sequencing.** Depends on #8811's row landing first — there is no row id to claim until then.
